title: Physical vs Logical Architecture Comparison
prompt: According to Azure architectural principles, how is physical architecture distinguished from logical architecture?

options.text: Physical architecture defines where Azure exists physically (datacenters, land, power), while logical architecture defines how resources are organized and managed (subscriptions, resource groups).
Physical architecture manages user passwords, while logical architecture connects optical fiber cables between cities.
Physical architecture refers exclusively to virtual machine operating systems, while logical architecture refers to network security groups.
Physical architecture is configured via JSON templates, while logical architecture cannot be modified once created.

explanation: Physical architecture represents tangible assets (buildings, servers, network cabling, power), while logical architecture represents management boundaries (Tenants, Management Groups, Subscriptions, Resource Groups).

title: Azure Region Definition
prompt: What is the official definition of an Azure Region?

options.text: A geographical area containing one or more datacenters connected through a dedicated, latency-defined network perimeter.
A single standalone physical server rack located in a customer data center.
A collection of Entra ID user accounts spanning an entire country.
A software container hosting multiple Docker microservices.

explanation: An Azure Region is a set of datacenters deployed within a latency-defined perimeter and connected through a dedicated regional low-latency network.

title: Key Benefits of Azure Regions
prompt: What are the main benefits of deploying workloads across Azure Regions? (Select TWO)

options.text: Data Residency and Compliance: Enables organizations to keep data close to users while adhering to local privacy laws.
Reduced Network Latency: Allows positioning applications physically closer to end users to improve response times.
Elimination of all Azure subscription billing charges.
Automatic conversion of Windows VMs into Linux containers without configuration.

explanation: Azure Regions provide local data residency compliance and reduced network latency by placing cloud resources near users.

title: Availability Zone Definition
prompt: Which statement accurately describes an Azure Availability Zone?

options.text: A physically separate datacenter location within an Azure region equipped with independent power, cooling, and networking infrastructure.
A virtual subnet within an Azure Virtual Network used for database isolation.
A backup copy of data saved automatically in a secondary country.
A security group rule that blocks incoming HTTP requests.

explanation: Availability Zones are unique physical locations within an Azure region. Each zone is made up of one or more datacenters with independent power, cooling, and networking.

title: Matching Azure Physical Infrastructure Components
prompt: Match each Azure physical infrastructure component to its correct architectural description.

targets.label: Latency-defined perimeter containing datacenters connected via dedicated low-latency fiber network.
Physically isolated datacenter facility within a region with independent power, cooling, and networking.
Two regions in the same geography paired at least 300 miles apart for disaster recovery.
A discrete market (typically containing two or more regions) that preserves data residency and compliance boundaries.

explanation: Azure Physical Architecture builds from Datacenters -> Availability Zones -> Regions -> Regional Pairs -> Geographies.

title: Azure Regional Pairs Distance & DR
prompt: How far apart are paired Azure Regions typically located, and why?

options.text: At least 300 miles apart, to prevent a single natural disaster or regional outage from affecting both paired regions simultaneously.
10 meters apart, to maximize cable connection speeds between racks.
Always in different continents, to enforce international border security policies.
Exactly 5 miles apart, to allow wireless microwave synchronization.

explanation: Regional Pairs are separated by at least 300 miles (where possible) to protect against regional disasters, power grid failures, or natural events.

title: Azure Entra ID Tenant Scope
prompt: What represents the top-level logical boundary for organization identity, users, and authentication in Azure?

options.text: Azure Entra ID (Azure AD) Tenant
Resource Group
Virtual Network Subnet
Storage Account Container

explanation: An Entra ID Tenant represents a dedicated, isolated instance of Entra ID that an organization receives when signing up for Microsoft cloud services.

title: Management Group Capabilities
prompt: Which of the following statements regarding Azure Management Groups are true? (Select TWO)

options.text: Management Groups provide a scope of governance above subscriptions, allowing policy assignments to inherit down the tree.
Management Group hierarchies can support up to 6 levels of depth for enterprise organizational modeling.
Management Groups store virtual machine OS hard drive disk files directly.
Deleting a Management Group permanently erases all underlying Virtual Machines instantly without recovery.

explanation: Management Groups allow hierarchical organization of subscriptions (up to 6 levels deep) to apply Azure Policy and RBAC rules uniformly.

title: Azure Subscriptions as Boundaries
prompt: An Azure Subscription acts as a fundamental logical boundary for which two key functions?

options.text: Billing Boundary (generating separate invoices/costs) and Access Control / Security Boundary.
Hardware RAM allocation and CPU clock speed regulation.
Physical fiber optic cable routing and diesel generator fueling schedules.
Web browser cookie storage and DNS domain registration.

explanation: Subscriptions serve as a billing container (where usage charges are grouped) and a management security boundary for RBAC and quotas.

title: Matching Azure Logical Hierarchy Levels
prompt: Match each Azure logical hierarchy scope to its correct management function.

targets.label: Highest organizational scope used to manage governance and policy compliance across multiple subscriptions.
Logical container providing billing separation and top-level administration boundary.
Logical container that holds related Azure assets deployed, managed, and deleted as a lifecycle unit.
Individual manageable item in Azure, such as a Virtual Machine, Storage Account, or SQL Database.

explanation: Azure Logical Hierarchy: Management Groups -> Subscriptions -> Resource Groups -> Resources.

title: Resource Group Rules & Properties
prompt: Which rule applies to Azure Resource Groups?

options.text: A resource can exist in only one Resource Group at a time.
Deleting a Resource Group retains all child Virtual Machines running indefinitely.
All resources in a Resource Group must be located in the exact same physical region as the Resource Group itself.
Resource Groups can be nested inside other Resource Groups up to 10 levels deep.

explanation: A resource belongs to exactly one Resource Group. Note that resources inside a Resource Group can reside in different Azure Regions than the group itself.

title: Azure Geographies & Data Residency
prompt: What is the purpose of an Azure Geography? (Select TWO)

options.text: To define a discrete market containing two or more Azure regions that preserve data residency and compliance boundaries.
To ensure that geopolitical boundaries are respected for tax, legal, and compliance regulations.
To force all virtual machines in the world to reboot simultaneously.
To automatically translate English source code into 50 languages.

explanation: Geographies contain two or more regions and ensure data residency, sovereignty, compliance, and latency boundaries are preserved.

title: Global vs Regional Azure Services
prompt: Which of the following is considered a Global Azure Service (not tied to a specific Azure Region)?

options.text: Azure Entra ID (Azure AD)
Azure Virtual Machine (IaaS VM)
Azure VNet Subnet
Azure Managed Disk

explanation: Azure Entra ID, Traffic Manager, Azure Front Door, and Azure DNS are Global services, whereas VMs, VNets, and Disks are Regional services.
